prompts.title: 男性 · 希腊雕塑
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a character turnaround concept sheet for an original fitness app; this character will later be modeled in 3D and rigged for strength-training demonstrations.
Art direction: a newly designed HUMAN FIGURE INSPIRED BY CLASSICAL ANCIENT GREEK MARBLE SCULPTURE. Quiet strength, harmonious athletic proportions, beautifully observed anatomy and classical facial planes, an elegant straight Greek nose, serene expression, sculpted unpainted eyes with subtle eyelid detail. A cohesive luminous ivory-white marble material for body, hair and garments, fine satin stone surface and extremely subtle grain, gentle sculptural tool softness. The surface should look like actual finely carved marble, not glossy plastic, a robot, an anatomical dummy or a white-painted living human. No cracks, damage, grime, obvious veins, metallic parts, seams at joints or colored accents. All fingers, arms and legs intact.
Composition: one large landscape modeling sheet containing exactly three full-body ORTHOGRAPHIC views of the SAME character at exactly the same scale: FRONT at left, exact RIGHT SIDE profile facing right at center, BACK at right. Equal ground baseline and consistent shoulder/hip/knee landmarks. Full figure from crown to toes with comfortable margins. No perspective, 3/4 view, alternate poses or extra inset details. These are three views of one coherent character, not three different sculptures.
Pose: neutral A-pose for modeling, shoulders relaxed, arms straight about 25–30 degrees away from the torso in the frontal plane, elbows almost straight, five natural fingers visible and slightly separated. Feet hip-width apart, both feet flat, knees softly straight and pelvis level. Side view is exactly the same A-pose seen from 90 degrees, not a different arm position. No contrapposto, raised heels or action pose.
Body: natural continuous muscle and joint transitions, clear but tasteful shoulder/chest/back/quadriceps/glute forms, practical athletic anatomy. Classical harmony rather than extreme bodybuilding. Bare feet. Sculpted garments sit close to the body, with shallow folds and no loose hanging cloth, so the silhouette remains legible for exercise demonstration. Preserve the feel of a Greek sculpture without adding robes that hide the limbs.
Presentation: warm medium-light gray studio background that gently contrasts with the ivory marble; very soft directional museum-studio illumination that shows the carved anatomy, faint ground contact shadow. No pedestal, columns, scenery, weapons, laurel wreath, jewelry, equipment, diagram arrows, modern logos or watermarks. A carefully finished original art-direction concept, not a photograph of an existing historical sculpture. Greek-influenced details, not a copy of a named sculpture.
Only small unobtrusive typography outside the figures: the specified title at upper left and "FRONT", "SIDE", "BACK" under the three views.
Subject: an adult male athlete approximately 28–35 years old with balanced 7.5-head-tall classical proportions, strong shoulders and upper back, developed but moderate pectorals, naturally defined abdomen, muscular glutes and thighs, graceful strong calves. A dignified classical face with a broad brow, straight nose and gently defined jaw, no beard. Short compact waves and small organized Greek-style curls carved close to the skull, completely in marble. Avoid a contemporary quiff, undercut or fashion hairstyle.
Clothing: bare torso and a simple modest fitted short athletic loin-wrap carved in the same marble, completely covering the pelvis and buttocks and ending high on the thigh. The wrap should have a clean secure waistband, a subtle diagonal fold at the front and very shallow drapery; visibly close-fitting short trunks under the wrap, without a dangling flap or a skirt. No visible genital detail. Most of each quadriceps remains uncovered.
Overall character: calm, disciplined and timeless, as if an ancient Greek athletic sculpture was purpose-designed as the male demonstrator for a contemporary fitness app.
Title verbatim: "G / GREEK ATHLETE — MALE".
